summary: A denser, more restrictive cousin of Agricola and Le Havre where you build out a personal tableau of production buildings on a small hex-based estate, converting raw resources through multi-step chains into high-value goods. The rondel resource system and tight building-placement puzzle create a heavier, more solitaire-feeling optimization game than Rosenberg's other titles, with real tension over land and building slots.
praised: Deep, satisfying production-chain puzzle with many viable strategies (peat/coal vs. grain/livestock economies)
Rondel mechanism elegantly controls resource availability without upkeep bookkeeping
High replayability from modular building decks and different starting maps
Strong sense of building an efficient personal engine
criticised: Very heavy rules overhead and long teach for new players
Multiplayer interaction is minimal, mostly a race for tiles/buildings rather than direct engagement
Analysis paralysis due to the number of building options and long-term planning required
Can feel dry or overly mechanical/spreadsheet-like compared to more thematic worker placement games

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light competition for shared buildings and rondel resources

scoring.why: Points come from a wide mix of buildings constructed, goods produced/converted, and end-game bonuses, rewarding overall economic efficiency rather than any single track
